answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (PoroTomo DAS, Brady Hot Springs, March 2016; stride 20), from `python3 ~/poro/agent/report.py <run>` (read-only; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20, covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, 3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b 0.9849 (34 above Mc)
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days (net extraction)
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED probability (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated one, from the LBNL catalogue):
  b      Sigma     P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0    -5.449    0.0001198      5.236e-06                   0.03719
  0.73   -5.319    0.004922       0.0002155                   0.2809
  0.65   -5.281    0.01474        0.0006484                   0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes — this is the upper bound, not calibrated; every DAS detection is counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b 0.9849, Sigma -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated (LBNL-catalogue) P(Mw>=5.5) per year is at most ~1.5e-2/yr (b=0.65), ~4.9e-3/yr (b=0.73), and ~1.2e-4/yr (b=1.0) — all far below the DAS-based upper bound of 0.07842/yr, which uses uncalibrated DAS magnitudes and over-counts, so a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is very unlikely on the calibrated estimate.
